research.notes:
WAVE 3 narrow rounding pass for the captioning/tagging lane. Did NOT re-list the already-cataloged JoyCaption Beta One, WD EVA02-Large v3, MiniCPM-V 4.5, InternVL3.5-8B, or Florence-2. Added the two requested WD v3 family members (SwinV2 + ConvNeXt — both confirmed distinct architectures, both Apache-2.0, both Danbooru cutoff 2024-02-28), CapRL-InternVL3.5-8B (confirmed real downloadable weights at internlm/CapRL-InternVL3.5-8B, weights license Apache-2.0; verified the 8B base uses Qwen3 which is ALSO Apache-2.0, so no Qwen-license inheritance — fully commercial-safe; note the training DATASET CapRL-2M/QA-75K is CC-BY-NC-4.0 but a data license does not bind users of the released weights or the captions they generate), and one genuinely-new strong 2025 entrant: Camie-Tagger v2 (143M ViT, 70,527 tags vs ~10k for WD — much broader vocab including artist/copyright/character; license is GPL-3.0, which is the one license caveat in this lane). LICENSE AXIS (decisive for both uses):
- WD SwinV2 v3 + WD ConvNeXt v3 + CapRL-InternVL3.5-8B = Apache-2.0 → unambiguously commercial-safe for game-asset tagging AND marketing. These are tools that LABEL your images; their output (tags/captions) is not a derivative work of the model, so even setting aside the permissive license, using them to caption a training set for a commercial LoRA carries no licensing encumbrance.
- Camie-Tagger v2 = GPL-3.0 (copyleft). Important nuance: GPL obligations attach to redistributing/modifying the MODEL, not to the tag output. Running it as an inference tool to caption your own dataset does not make the dataset or resulting LoRA a GPL derivative (mere output is not a derivative work under GPL). So it remains practically commercial-safe AS A TAGGING TOOL — flagged 'conditional' only to be honest about the copyleft on the weights themselves should the user bundle/redistribute the model. This is why commercial_use is set to 'conditional' for it and 'yes' for the Apache trio. THROUGHPUT on RTX 5090 / 32 GB (all fit easily):
- WD v3 taggers (SwinV2 98M / ConvNeXt 98.7M, ONNX or timm): classifier-style, <2 GB VRAM, batched throughput in the hundreds of images/sec. Booru-tag output (rating + character + general) — the canonical SDXL/Illustrious/NoobAI/Pony prompt-style tagging.
- Camie-Tagger v2 (143M ViT): <2 GB VRAM, fast batched inference; its 70k-tag vocabulary is the reason to reach for it over WD when you need fine-grained artist/copyright/meta tags for an Illustrious or NoobAI LoRA.
- CapRL-InternVL3.5-8B: full 8B VLM, ~9 GB weights at BF16 (model card states ~9 GB) + KV cache; runs comfortably on 32 GB via vLLM (--gpu_memory_utilization=0.95). This is the PROSE/dense-caption specialist (fine-grained objects, attributes, OCR, relations, events) — the right tool for Flux/Qwen-Image LoRAs that train on natural-language captions rather than booru tags. ICLR 2026 paper; captioning quality reported to beat Qwen2.5-VL-72B at 8B. best_for split per the lane brief: WD SwinV2/ConvNeXt v3 + Camie v2 → booru tagging for SDXL/Illustrious LoRAs (use-tag game-asset). CapRL → prose captioning for Flux/Qwen LoRAs (use-tag both — also strong for marketing alt-text / product descriptions). WD ConvNeXt is the slightly lower-F1 sibling of SwinV2 (0.4419 vs 0.4541 macro-F1) — kept as a distinct row per the brief; in practice WD-EVA02-Large v3 (already cataloged) > SwinV2 ≈ ViT-Large > ConvNeXt within the family, so ConvNeXt is 'situational' (ensemble / second-opinion tagging) while SwinV2 is the recommended mid-tier WD default.

models.summary: An RL-tuned dense-caption specialist and a strong genuinely-new (Oct 2025) addition to this lane. CapRL is the first application of Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards to open-ended captioning: captions are rewarded by how well a text-only model can answer visual questions using ONLY the generated caption, which pushes the model toward comprehensive, low-hallucination, structured prose (fine-grained objects, attributes, OCR, relations, events). Built on InternVL3.5-8B as policy; reported to beat Qwen2.5-VL-72B on captioning quality at 8B. This is the PROSE/natural-language captioner for Flux / Qwen-Image LoRA datasets (and excellent for marketing alt-text and product descriptions) — the complement to the WD/Camie booru taggers. LICENSE / COMMERCIAL-SAFETY IS THE DECISIVE AXIS — key finding for this lane: (1) HiDream-E1 / E1.1 carry a license NUANCE that materially affects commercial-safety for game-asset work. The HiDream transformer weights are MIT (clean, permissive). BUT the model ships a meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct text encoder governed by the Llama 3.1 Community License — NOT Apache/MIT. Llama 3.1 Community License permits commercial use but has conditions: (a) attribution ("Built with Llama"), (b) the >700M-monthly-active-users clause requiring a separate license from Meta, and (c) acceptable-use policy. For a solo/indie game studio this is commercially usable, but it is NOT unconditionally permissive the way Apache-2.0 is. I set commercial_use = "conditional" for both HiDream editors and flagged this explicitly. The official HF cards say "You own all content you create with this model... use freely" — output ownership is clean; the constraint is on the model components, not the generated images. Game-asset fit is therefore good (you own the sprites/concepts you generate) but the license is a notch below the fully-clean Apache editors. (2) Qwen-Image-Edit-2509, FireRed-Image-Edit-1.1, and LongCat-Image-Edit are ALL Apache-2.0 (FireRed explicitly states "code AND weights" Apache-2.0; Qwen-2509 inherits Qwen-Image Apache-2.0; LongCat HF card license tag = apache-2.0). extras.name: ComfyUI-WD14-Tagger (pythongosssss)
extras.note: PRIMARY TARGET. The de-facto booru-tag captioner node for ComfyUI. Interrogates images and emits comma-separated Danbooru/booru tags via SmilingWolf's WD v1.4 ONNX tagger models (ConvNextV2 is the most popular, MOAT/ViT/SwinV2 also selectable; models auto-download to models/wd14_tagger at runtime, onnxruntime dependency). Node added via image -> 'WD14 Tagger|pysssss'; also right-click 'WD14 Tagger' on any LoadImage/Preview/SaveImage node for one-off interrogation. Supports batched inputs and threshold/character-threshold/exclude-tag controls — exactly what you want for bulk LoRA dataset captioning. License: MIT (confirmed via repo). pyproject version 1.0.1; repo last pushed 2025-07-11, ~1.2k stars — current and stable. COMMERCIAL-SAFE node (the tagger weights are SmilingWolf's, released for open use). This is the canonical tagging half of a game-asset LoRA dataset pipeline on a 5090/32GB — tagging is CPU/ONNX-light, no VRAM concern. Verified 2026-06-02.

extras.name: audio-separation-nodes-comfyui (christian-byrne)
extras.note: Stem-separation node: splits an audio track into 4 stems (vocals / drums / bass / other) using torchaudio's Hybrid Demucs (HDEMUCS_HIGH_MUSDB). Also does tempo-match, crop/slice, and a recombine node to further isolate (e.g. guitar lives in 'other'). Pairs naturally with Wan2.2-S2V (feed an isolated vocal stem as the audio driver for lip-sync). License: MIT (confirmed via GitHub API). v2.0.0 released ~2026-04-13, repo last pushed 2026-04-14, ~570 stars — actively maintained and current. COMMERCIAL-SAFE (MIT node; Demucs weights are MIT/research-permissive via torchaudio). Trivial VRAM on a 5090. Doubles as the stem-separation workflow source below. Verified 2026-06-02.

extras.name: was-node-suite-comfyui (ltdrdata-maintained fork)
extras.note: Essential general-purpose suite (210+ nodes): image batch/dataset prep (Load Image Batch, Image Batch, Image Save with filename templating), text/caption parsing (CLIPTextEncode NSP, wildcards/noodle-soup), latent/noise utilities, logic/switch nodes, and the Bus node for tidying graphs. MAINTENANCE NOTE (load-bearing): the original WASasquatch/was-node-suite-comfyui repo was ARCHIVED read-only on 2025-06-02 (author retired); the live fork is now maintained by ltdrdata (ComfyUI-Manager author) at github.com/ltdrdata/was-node-suite-comfyui — point your install there. License: MIT. COMMERCIAL-SAFE. The Load-Image-Batch + Image-Save pairing is a workhorse for building/exporting game-asset datasets. Verified 2026-06-02.

extras.name: Image-Captioning-in-ComfyUI (LarryJane491) — LoRA Caption Load/Save
extras.note: The dataset-side complement to WD14-Tagger: provides 'LoRA Caption Load' (pulls every image from a folder) and 'LoRA Caption Save' (writes a matching.txt caption file next to each image — the exact layout Kohya_ss / OneTrainer expect for LoRA training). Note: it does NOT caption on its own — the WD14 Tagger node is mandatory in-graph to actually produce the tags; this pack only handles batch load + per-file.txt save. License: NOT STATED in repo (no LICENSE file detected) — flag for commercial use; safe to run locally, but treat distribution/licensing as unclear. Small repo (~5 commits) but the load/save pattern is the standard booru-tag dataset export. Verified 2026-06-02.

extras.name: ComfyUI_Comfyroll_CustomNodes (Suzie1) — LICENSE UNCLEAR
extras.note: Useful 175-node QoL/utility suite (CR Aspect Ratio, LoRA Stack/Loader, Multi-ControlNet stack, text-overlay/graphics, model-merge, animation scheduling). COMMERCIAL FLAG (decisive axis): repo has NO LICENSE file at root — GitHub's license API returns none, and there is no LICENSE/LICENSE.txt — so its terms are genuinely UNSTATED. Also stale: last pushed 2024-07-24 (~2 yrs), v1.76, unmaintained. Fine for local convenience, but do NOT rely on it for commercial-distribution certainty and prefer rgthree / KJNodes / WAS (already cataloged or above) for the same QoL where licensing matters. Listed for completeness with the flag, not as a clean recommendation. Verified 2026-06-02.

extras.name: efficiency-nodes-comfyui (jags111 fork)
extras.note: Workflow-condensing pack: Efficient KSampler (combines loader+sampler+VAE-decode into one node), XY Plot (grid sweeps over seeds/CFG/steps/samplers/checkpoints/LoRAs — handy for dialing in a consistent game-asset look), and LoRA/ControlNet stackers. MAINTENANCE NOTE: original LucianoCirino repo is explicitly no-longer-maintained; the live fork is jags111/efficiency-nodes-comfyui (slow but active). License: GPL-3.0 (per repo). COMMERCIAL note: GPL-3.0 covers the node CODE, not the images you generate — generated outputs are unaffected, so it is commercial-safe for asset production; only matters if you redistribute the node code itself. Verified 2026-06-02.

extras.name: Audio Separation (stem split) — official ComfyUI example workflow
extras.note: STEM-SEPARATION workflow. Official comfy.org example built on christian-byrne's audio-separation-nodes (above): LoadAudio -> AudioSeparation (Hybrid Demucs) -> per-stem PreviewAudio/SaveAudio for vocals/drums/bass/other. Importable JSON, no extra weights beyond the auto-downloaded Demucs checkpoint. Vetted/first-party. The repo's own README example workflows (isolate-vocals, replace-BGM, instrumental-extract) are the secondary source. Verified 2026-06-02.

extras.name: LoRA Caption (booru-tag dataset captioning) workflow — Weird Wonderful AI Art
extras.note: BOORU-TAG DATASET CAPTIONING workflow. End-to-end ComfyUI graph: LoRA Caption Load -> WD14 Tagger -> LoRA Caption Save, writing per-image.txt booru-tag files ready for Kohya_ss/OneTrainer LoRA training. Uses the two nodes above (LarryJane491 + pythongosssss WD14). Well-known community walkthrough with the downloadable workflow and step-by-step. For higher caption quality, pair with the Florence2+WD14 hybrid pattern (Florence2 for natural-language scene description, WD14 for concrete attributes — clothing/hair/eye color) since Florence2 is already cataloged. Verified 2026-06-02.

extras.name: Wan2.2-S2V Audio-Driven Video — official ComfyUI native workflow
extras.note: WAN-S2V workflow. First-party ComfyUI tutorial + downloadable JSON for Wan2.2-S2V (sound/speech-to-video): one reference image + an audio clip -> lip-synced/expressive video. Pipeline: UNETLoader + CLIPLoader + VAELoader + AudioEncoderLoader(wav2vec2) -> WanSoundImageToVideo -> KSampler -> VAEDecode -> VHS_VideoCombine (muxes original audio). Models: wan2.2_s2v_14B_fp8_scaled (LOWER-VRAM, fits 32GB comfortably) or _bf16 (quality); umt5_xxl_fp8 text encoder; wan_2.1_vae; wav2vec2_large_english_fp16 audio encoder. Optional Lightning LoRA for speed (warns of dynamics/quality loss). Requires VideoHelperSuite (already cataloged) for VHS_VideoCombine. Feed it an isolated vocal stem from the audio-separation node above for cleaner lip-sync. A GGUF/lower-VRAM community variant exists on Civitai (SarcasticTOFU WAN2.2_S2V_Img2Vid) if you need to go below fp8. Verified 2026-06-02.
